# Markitai: Agent guide

> Development version 1.3.0-dev. Stable 1.3.0 is not yet published. This guide is plain Markdown and is included in CLI archives for offline use.

Markitai reads local documents and images or HTTP(S) pages, then writes
Markdown and extracted assets. The CLI needs no Python, Node.js or Go runtime;
Node/Python/Go bindings require their respective runtimes. Native readers have
format and fidelity limits. A recognized extension is not a promise of full
layout preservation. [Quick start](docs/quickstart.md) lists the 61 extensions,
installation steps and platform backends.

## Use authorized inputs and explicit output paths

Prefer an absolute executable path and a task-specific output directory. Set
`MARKITAI_HOME` to a separate state directory before starting the process when
a task should not share configuration, caches or history. The normal default
is `~/.markitai`. Configuration search includes the current working directory
and environment; isolation requires controlling those inputs as well. Do not
supply private files, credential values or external destinations without the
caller's authorization.

For a plain local conversion:

```sh
markitai /absolute/path/report.docx -o /absolute/path/output --no-llm --json
```

On Windows use `markitai.exe` and Windows absolute paths. Archives also provide
`mkai` / `mkai.exe` and `markitai-mcp` / `markitai-mcp.exe`. Shell PATH changes
in an interactive profile might not apply to an Agent process, so configure
the executable's full path.

## CLI machine output

Use `-o` with `--json`; the CLI then writes a JSON result envelope to stdout,
with diagnostics on stderr. `--json` without `-o` is a usage error. Without
`--json` or `-o`, stdout is document Markdown and asset references can be
persistent absolute `file://` URIs under Markitai state. Do not infer
successful conversion from empty stdout. Read top-level `ok` / `error`, each
item's `status` / `skip_reason`, written paths and warnings in the envelope. A
standalone image without OCR or LLM extraction is skipped as `image_only`.

Exit codes: 0 for success (including supported skips), 1 for a single failure,
2 for invalid arguments (also provider batch still pending), and 10 for batch
item failures. Argument errors can occur before the JSON envelope is created; inspect stderr and the exit code.
Batch reports under `output/.markitai/reports/` supplement stdout and do not
replace it. Use explicit conflict policy when retries matter; the default is
`rename`, not overwrite. `--pure` disables generated frontmatter and model
processing. Read [CLI](docs/cli.md) for the exact envelope and overrides.

## MCP

Launch `markitai mcp` or `markitai-mcp` (`.exe` on Windows) over stdio. Normal
protocol messages use stdout; diagnostics use stderr. No HTTP MCP endpoint is
added. Give the MCP host the actual executable path and, when needed, a
separate `MARKITAI_HOME` and configuration file; see [MCP](docs/mcp.md).

The four tools are:

- `convert_document`: absolute local `path` (`~` is expanded); an ordinary directory is not a document. Modern `.numbers` packages are supported as a single document.
- `convert_url`: an HTTP(S) URL, which can require a network request or browser.
- `batch_convert`: a nonempty list of local paths and/or URLs; returns a job ID.
- `job_status`: poll that ID in the same MCP server process while `running`, then inspect each item and the `failed` count. Terminal status is `completed` or `cancelled`; completion can include failed items.

Single-source tools accept `output_dir`, `llm`, `ocr`, `screenshot`, `alt`,
`desc` and `profile`. Omitted/null feature flags follow configuration; use
explicit false when the task must disable them. `output_dir` must be absolute;
omitted/null/empty creates a retained temporary directory. The caller must
clean it up after consuming the results, including after server shutdown.

Successful results include `structuredContent` and a JSON text block. Read
`markdown_file` for the complete output when `truncated` is true; the inline
body is only a preview for long documents. Keep the output directory while
using its assets/screenshots. Expected conversion errors carry `isError: true`.
Do not parse human progress text as a tool result. Output schemas and the
full field inventory are in [MCP](docs/mcp.md).

## Offline and optional components

Plain local text/document conversion does not require provider access. On
macOS the default OCR backend is Vision; Windows/Linux use local Paddle and
built-in hayro PDF rendering. Paddle ONNX models are not included in archives.
`markitai doctor --json` only inspects readiness; `doctor --fix` can download
missing models and repair safely managed corrupt models. Prepare them before
an offline task. Normal OCR does not silently overwrite corrupt models, and
unsafe model paths are rejected. Never respond to an unsafe-path error by
blindly enabling repair.

HEIF/AVIF decoding uses macOS ImageIO and is unsupported on Windows/Linux in
this build. JavaScript pages/screenshots need Chrome/Chromium. Office page
images and OCR supplements need LibreOffice; native text readers do not.
Model enhancement (`--llm`, captions/descriptions) uses configured providers
or subscription runtimes and can send content externally. `--no-llm` disables
that model step. `--no-remote-fetch` prevents third-party fetch services; it
is not an OS network sandbox and still permits direct HTTP(S) downloads and
browser requests. An offline workflow must also avoid URL inputs, remote
resources and unprepared components.

Batch `--resume` is available on macOS, Linux and Windows for directory and
`.urls` batches. A single file or URL cannot be resumed. Windows Go/cgo
installed-package acceptance is unverified. Do not turn availability of a
CLI command into a claim of complete format, quality, performance or binding
parity. [CLI](docs/cli.md) lists remaining migration gaps.

## More detail

Read [README](README.md), [quick start](docs/quickstart.md), [CLI](docs/cli.md)
and [MCP](docs/mcp.md) offline in the archive. The [index](docs/index.md) links
the full source documentation; other topics require the repository checkout.
